evidence: Read the full diff. The only change in schema.go is the location pattern. It goes from ^[^:\s]+:[1-9][0-9]*(-[1-9][0-9]*)?$ to ^.+:[1-9][0-9]*(-[1-9][0-9]*)?$.

engine/reviewresult/rules.go:174 has locationPattern ^.+:[1-9][0-9]*(?:-[1-9][0-9]*)?$. The two differ only in a capturing group versus a non-capturing group, so they match the same strings. In Go RE2 and in ECMA-262, `.` does not match a newline, and `$` anchors at the end of the text.
The Go raw string for the schema has no backslash left in the location pattern. The old \\s escape is gone, so there is no JSON escaping problem.

The test asserts the exact schema pattern string. It then checks that both the schema pattern, compiled with Go regexp, and the parser's locationPattern accept 'docs/my file.md:3' and 'a:b.go:4-7'. This covers the space and colon cases the commit describes.
The test rename to TestSchemaIdAndLocationPatterns describes what it checks and drops the stale 'BenchSent' wording.
